Simpsons Comics Barn Burner (2005, Collected Edition)

works.overview: Mr. Burns tests his Rejuvenator Ray on Homer Simpson, resulting in Homer growing to colossal proportions.
Principal Skinner sends Bart to Springfield State Prison to be Scared Spitless, Springfield's version of Scared Straight. Bart gets stuck in a cell with his nemesis... Sideshow Bob.
The Springfield Puma has been stolen, and it's up to Bart and Lisa to solve the crime.
Bart gets revenge on a baseball player who gets him and Milhouse ejected from the game.
The residents of Springfield gain super-powers after a nuclear explosion, and it's up to Bartman to find out why.
Lisa joins Otto's band, Otto and the Screaming Whiners.
Simpsons go to the circus.
Homer is tricked into shrinking down and clearing an internal blockage in Mr. Burns body.
Lisa becomes a best selling author after Bart changes her diary.
Mr. Burns uses the Simpsons to smuggle a secret energy source into the country.
Ned Flanders goes bad.
Bart and Milhouse have their comic book creation, the Oysterizer, stolen by some comic book creators they meet at a comic convention.
Homer befriends a hobo who is in reality the owner of Duff Beer. When the hobo allegedly dies, Homer inherits a fortune, to the dismay of the owner of the other 49% of Duff Beer... Mr. Burns.

Grampa Simpson tells a story about life before television. However, his story incorporates a bunch of television shows such as: Beverly Hills 90210, The Waltons, The Brady Bunch, The Partridge Family and Leave it to Beaver.
Patty and Selma lose their jobs and are forced to move in with Marge's family. They find a new job, as stewardesses.
Rainier Wolfcastle comes to Springfield to force the town to lose weight.
For a school report, Bart makes it so that the statue of Jebediah Springfield cries and Lisa discovers what's happened.
Mr. Burns gives Apu on offer he can't refuse... a new Mega Kwik-E Super Store.
Bart, Milhouse and Krusty go to France.
The Presidential candidates come to Springfield.
Lisa and Martin have a poetry battle.
Professor Frink is transported to an alternate universe Springfield where Marge is mayor and Sideshow Bob is the school principal.
Homer has his former college roommates stay over in the basement.
Grandpa is sick of being ignored and starts a new career in graffiti.

A visit to the Simpson house results in a painful, yet hilarious, injury to Krusty, so he becomes a houseguest. This leaves the Simpsons to fend off a flock of lawyers by broadcasting the show from their own home.

In the Krusty Brand Fun Factory, all your brand name dreams come true, so of course Bart and Homer will do anything to get into it. But a mysterious presence convinces Bart and Homer they won't escape the Krusty Brand Deathtrap.

Homer became a celebrity through his appearances on all those bleep, blunder, and blooper shows, so now everyone wants to know when Homer will say "D'oh!" The rest of the world is in on the gag of The Homer Show, except of course Homer Simpson.
Does Brain Freeze Steve, who rumor has it that his head exploded when he drank a squishee with two straws, still haunt the Kwik-E-Mart?
Bart manages to use the yearbook staff's mimeograph to give Lisa Simpson and Martin Prince positions as substitute teachers at Springfield Elementary.
Santa's Little Helper is the top dog of fast food franchises, but what good is celebrity, wealth, and power without the boy you love?

Sideshow Bob has been released from jail, but while working as a dog groomer/VCR repairman he becomes the mastermind of a crime school which includes Jimbo, Dolph, Kearney, Nelson, and Bart Simpson as a students.  Bart leads them all on a merry chase all over Springfield.

A story set thirty years in the future Bart Simpson is going to die, unless he receives radical transplant surgery.  But his last conscious utterance, "Fish logs...", bears on the situation and only Lisa can unlock the secret.
Homer puts his life in danger after an accidental appearance on a dating game show causes a rift with Marge and causes Homer to enter a more dangerous game to prove his love.
Lisa discovers an insidious plot against the youth of Springfield after she runs afoul of the new baby-sitters union and Maggie gets lost in the red tape of organized labor.
A battle between Upper Springfield and Lower Springfield over the water supply.

It's Thanksgiving as only the Simpsons can celebrate it, with Lisa protesting the annual turkey-cide, Bart running off to the Try 'N' Save, Homer trying to save Mr. Burns from genetically-engineered turkeys, and Marge left with nothing to serve her guests.
Every kid in Springfield wants the new Itchy & Scratchy Interactive Playset for Christmas, but Comic Book Guy has cornered the market.
Homer, Carl, Lenny, and Barney form the Beer Boys to "help" Moe behind the bar when Moe's gallbladder goes on the fritz.
Homer drives a tank to work, where his lousy parking job fuels a revenge war that sends Springfield, and maybe the whole planet, hurtling toward the brink of destruction.
A swimming pool contractor comes to claim the Ned Flanders’ pool that was accidentally dug in Homer's yard, moving Homer to barricade himself and half of Springfield in his backyard.
Will Smithers turn out to be the heir to the throne of Sweden?
When Bart turns tattletale on Dolph, Jimbo, Kearney, and Nelson on national TV, he becomes the target of death threats.
When Mayor Quimby bans alcohol on Sunday's, Homer decides Springfield needs a new mayor... him!
Homer forms a group from the boys of Springfield, to cash in on the current "boy band" phenomenon, but they have no discernable talent or singing ability...except for Ralph Wiggum.
Waylon Smithers and Marge Simpson wage a battle for the love and devotion of Homer.
Bart ends up in control of Springfield's print media, so he prints news that suits him.  But the articles soon go out of control, leaving half of Springfield is in ruins.
Since the Sunday school teacher called in sick, Bart offers to tell Rod and Todd his version of the bible stories.
Mr. Burns wants to build a new golf course in the middle of the Springfield Natural Preserve, but the Li'l Chickadees group won't let him get away with it.
Marge is hired as a judge on a TV show.
The Simpsons win an all-expenses paid trip to the remote Latin American country of Bosqueverde, where Bart leads the rebel forces in a military coup.
Homer starts his own cruise ship business.
Ned, Apu, and Comic Book Guy form a vigilante group to combat shoplifting in Springfield.
Homer tells stories about The Gods.
Cecil is tired of being underappreciated, so he targets Lisa Simpson for death.
An eccentric collector looks for an heir for his collection, and the kids prepare for the annual school candy sale.
Krusty becomes the town doctor.  Homer loses his taste buds.
While Springfield's children perform Shakespeare's "Troilus and Cressida", Homer dozes off, dreaming of different Shakespeare "plays" portrayed by various Springfield residents.
Sideshow Bob has been released from prison again and may be disguised as one of three seemingly innocent visitors to Springfield in his quest to destroy Bart Simpson.
Grampa Simpson tells mixed-up Christmas stories, such as man-eating fruitcakes and Bart the Red-nosed Reindeer.
Every citizen of Springfield has a tale to tell about the Unemployment Office.
Homer Simpson and Ned Flanders appear on a reality TV show and trade places, houses, and more...and like it.

Homer receives a radioactive spider bite after an accident at the nuclear power plant that also injures Bart and Milhouse.  Homer is fired and begins work at the Lard Lad Donut Factory and may be the only person who can save Springfield from an economic crisis.
When Superintendent Chalmers is fired and Principal Skinner is promoted, who does the Springfield School Board hire to run Springfield Elementary?
When the Simpsons family become the trendsetters for the world, when will it all blow up in their faces?
With Grampa's training (as a former surfin' stuntman), Bart enters a surfing competition, and a freak tsunami sends Bart and Grampa on the ride of their lives.
The story of how one political animal, Snowball II, took on city hall and won.
The Simpsons travel to Scotland with Groundskeeper Willie, where Willie and his brother try to settle an age-old feud in a legendary groundskeeping tournament.

Lisa is diagnosed with complications due to Middle Child Syndrome, so the Simpsons adopt Nelson Muntz to balance things out.  But Nelson soon becomes head of the household and Homer suffers from Displaced Dad Syndrome.
Homer takes Lisa's class on a tour of America.
After a disaster at the nuclear power plant, Mr. Burns must house the whole town at Burns Manor because it is the only place above the poisonous mushroom cloud.
Homer buys a Krusty Burger franchise but discovers that trying to placate Krusty's rules ruins his efforts.
To fix the local economy Springfield excogitates a 24/7 working schedule for everyone.
Homer's get-rich-quick schemes convince Marge to get a life coach.
After messing up a school event Bart and Lisa must enter a pen pal program with third world children.

Bart and Lisa discover that there is a comic book about the Simpsons (in fact, they discover they are in #100). Homer reads about himself in #1. Only comic book guy can explain why there are comics about so many of the residents of Springfield. Issue includes ads from KrustyCO, many references to real and imaginary Bongo publications, and a visit to Springfield Comic-Con. Parodies include: Hercules; The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe; Jabberwocky; Julius Caesar; Scrooge McDuck and his nephews. The story ends with revelations about what mothers do with kids' old toys and comic collections.
Lisa tries to teach the readers about bees.
Dr. Nick helps Selma and Patty fix a hair problem.
Maggie Simpson and Moe Szyslak solve a museum robbery.
After Mr. Burns wastes millions on an unsuccessful advertising campaign to make him more popular, he creates a reality TV show where the winner will take over Mr. Burns' job for a day.
Bart draws a comic book with Homer wiping out on a roller skate. Will life imitate art as Homer approaches the top of the stairs and the waiting roller skate.
Bart and Milhouse go camping with Milhouse's mom and her new boyfriend, Bob the RV Salesman.

Homer orders a mobility scooter and starts using it. But because it is made for the handicapped, everyone thinks that Homer is disabled and he starts to use their benefits, after Mr. Burns gives him early retirement with full pay.

When Marge Simpson fails to get rid of old junk from the attic, she gets a tip from Lisa Simpson to sell them on eBuy. Marge becomes so addicted to selling stuff online she sells everything they own, unknowingly to Artie Ziff, so the family must move in with Grampa.
The Japanese version of the Simpsons.

After a nuclear plant accident forces a radioactive cloud into the atmosphere, Homer finds himself alone and still quite oversized in a very different and much more slender city. What is the secret behind his morbid obesity? Water retention? Big bones? A secret stash of pork rinds? Whatever it is, Homer may be humanity's last link to the fat gene and Springfield's last chance to avoid wasting away to skin and bones. Gangway for weight gain this December!

When a torrential rainstorm threatens to raise the level of Springfield River and destroy Springfield's crumbling levees, only one outspoken environmental advocate, only one eco-aware tree-hugging activist, only one global-warming truth-telling second grader can save the town from disaster - Lisa Simpson! Enjoy a cautionary tale from Springfield this January - before it's too late!

After watching one infomercial too many, Homer comes up with the bird-brained idea of raising ostriches to supplement his income. But when it's time to sell his feathered friends at the meat market, Homer would rather hide his head in the sand. The Simpsons will leave you in 'striches.

When Duff Industries introduces New Duff Beer, Homer Simpson, consummate consumer and connoisseur of fine, fair, and otherwise fermented fluids, determines that it tastes less than great and is decidedly less filling because he refuses to drink it. Join Homer as he enlists Barney, Duffman, and Surly of the Seven Duffs in a search that takes him to the heart of the tropical rainforests in order to get the hops back in his step and back into his favorite beer!
Ragin' Abe answers faux letters from readers (who actually created war comics for DC Comics) - R. Heath, J. Kubert, R. Kanigher and J. Severin.
Homer and Bart find Grampa's old comic books and open a comic book store. Homer begins to behave like Comic Book Guy, who is forced to close his shop.
When Marge saves Agnes wallet from being stolen by Snake while roller-skating, she joins The Springfield Spitfires and gets trained by the legendary Mary Tyler.

For the school science fair, Lisa makes a project about her relationship with her family and does a DNA test, which reveals her mother is a Hollander named Greta Vanglooten. Meanwhile Bart and Milhouse are trying to stay awake for two weeks as their experiment for the fair.
The Simpsons cast in "The Little Mermaid."

Krusty finds out that it is the pig's participation in the commercial that made The Clogger a success, and offers one million dollars to the person who brings the pig back. Homer refuses to give back Plopper after he discovered that, upon hearing about the reward, Bart and Lisa collected him from the forest.

Darcy Michael becomes the school's new chef and he begins to serve healthy food, to Lisa's joy, but when Michael gets her banned from lunch, she becomes Professor Frink's assistant on his TV show just to be able to eat lunch from television's vegetarian lunch buffet. Bart begins to smuggle sweets and fatty foods into the school, which he sells at expensive prices to the students.

After Homer ruins the family's washing machine, he and Bart and Grampa take the family's washing to the laundromat. Chaos ensues when Homer hands off the chore to Bart and Bart takes the opportunity to pull a prank which gets them into trouble with the laundromat's manager.

When the Simpsons discover a bee infestation in their home, they are determined to have the buzzing insects exterminated - until they taste the sweet, sweet honey produced by the hive! Then, they make themselves busy as bees building up their new honey business.
In July 2194, a tour guide takes us on a tour of The Simpsons Museum.

Patty and Selma are humiliated when Channel 6 News announces that Springfield has been named the ugliest city in America, and Kent Brockman shows pictures of them to explain how the city earned the designation. Marge tries to console her sisters and they challenge her to walk a mile in their shoes. Marge takes them up on the challenge and is shocked by the difference in how she's treated. Marge then starts a protest movement to stop discrimination against ugly people.

The Mayor declares a "Take Your Parent to Work Day," which results in Bart matching practical joke with Agnes Skinner and Homer and Mr. Burns thinking they are brothers when Abe Simpson marries an actress disguised as Mr. Burns mother.
Homer searches for a fuel efficient car.
Homer tries to cheat to win a bike race.
The judge orders Snake to live with the Simpsons until he is rehabilitated.
Loki's practical joke causes the apocalypse.
There's a new "kid" in school, and he's a better Bart than the real Bart.
Lisa writes a song that makes everyone nicer.
The Simpsons listen to three audiobooks.

Homer decides to start another get-rich-quick scheme, this time by selling Christmas trees. However things take a turn for the worse, as Birch Barlow, also looking to cash in over the holidays, does an inspiring rant about the "War on Christmas", putting Homer's business at risk.

While Lisa's best humanitarian instincts lead her to restore an injured owl to health, Homer's base behavior towards his fellow man intrigues Mr. Burns, who takes advantage of those qualities in a 'get rich quick' real estate scheme.

As the penalty for destroying Disco Stu's beta tapes, Homer must tell him three stories set in the 1970s. Homer tells him parodies of The Muppet Show, Little House on the Prairie and The Rockford Files.
While unconscious due to a combination of the flu and an overdose of flu medicine, Homer dreams of a world without beer.
Lenny gets hooked on Scifiometry, and Homer and the crew must rescue him from the cult.

After Bart plays a prank on Principal Skinner, Skinner orders Bart to let Ralph be his conscience and Ralph begins giving Bart advice everywhere he goes. Meanwhile, Marge begins selling a cleaner that has been in her family for generations and Homer helps her when they start to do commercials on TV.
After Lisa, by mistake, brings peanuts to school, she is forced to participate in a ballet performance along with Ralph to not be expelled, with the ballet's director being Sideshow Bob.
Homer blows up the internet.
Lisa takes a job at King Toot's Music Store. Meanwhile, Homer discovers that Ned Flanders helped record his and Marge's favorite song, causing Homer to have difficulties getting into a romantic mood.

Homer accidentally invents the most powerful vacuum cleaner on Earth and teams up with door-to-door salesman Gil Gunderson to peddle his wares. Meanwhile, when Bart and his pals get in trouble and are assigned to help out Groundskeeper Willie, the school handyman has enough extra time on his hands to earn his GED and teacher's credential. In no time, he becomes Springfield Elementary's most sought after substitute teacher.
The Comic Book Guy falls asleep and has a dream where the characters in SF movies look like the Simpsons.

After a run-in with the paparazzi, Krusty the Clown hires Homer to stand in for him, or rather, stand next to him -- because Homer makes Krusty look good by comparison. Meanwhile, Lisa becomes a stand-in studio musician for Bleeding Gums Murphy's sister, Flossy Murphy.
Ned opens a new bar, Ned's. And Moe doesn't like competition.
Marge takes the tag off the mattress and gets hauled off to jail.
When job offers keep coming his way, Homer is inspired to start an employment agency and pass the job offers on to other residents of Springfield.

When Homer wrecks the family car, he's forced to drive an upscale loaner car.  The car proves to be such an upgrade over their previous car, and life, that the family tries to come up with a way to keep it when their old car is ready.  And Mr. Burns has a moat built around his mansion.
Bart and Lisa sneak into a closed theme park and must dodge both the security guards and the gang of bullies who also are in the park illegally.
When Krusty is incapacitated due to a freak microwave accident, Lisa is recruited to replace him on air.  But a tip from an unlikely source reveals to Bart the real reason for Lisa's success.
Lisa's attempt to free Moe from prison via a podcast works in one respect: Since it got people to actually listen to Lisa, everyone in Springfield starts their own podcast.
When Bart learns that criminals sometimes discard hot merchandise in dumpsters to avoid being caught, he decides to scour the city's dumpsters in search of treasure.
Bart is recruited to play Itchy in the traveling stage production "Itchy & Scratchy Live".
Bart and Milhouse start a leaf-raking business.
Chief Wiggum's crusade to learn the secret identities of all the costumed vigilantes in Springfield wind up pitting Bartman against everyone, including his sidekick Houseboy.
Homer consumes a doughnut containing forty percent of his body weight in sugar and gains bizarre new abilities.
Homer gets lost in a museum exhibit and thinks he's been shrunk down to microscopic size.
Homer gets Bart tickets to the "Krusty on Ice" show for Christmas and Bart is less than thrilled.
Marge takes the family on a surprise trip to a mountain cabin that's all too familiar to Homer, and one of his deepest, darkest secrets is revealed.
In order to keep Sherri and Terri from exposing Bart's secret identity, Lisa begins appearing as Bartman and is immediately better at it than Bart was.
Homer mistakes Otto's car for his ride home and gets the wild night of his life.
Lisa takes a local coffee house to court for charging her a huge fee for use of their wi-fi signal. When she loses, the family is forced to open a coffee bar in their living room to pay the debt.
Homer joins the stress-reducing, adult coloring book craze, but before long his new daily obsession begins to creep into his dream life.
Krusty the Clown has acquired the rights to remake the Radioactive Man film and plans, to Bart's horror, to recast Radioactive Man and Fallout Boy as females.
Lisa tells a mystery story based on Murder on the Orient Express.

Grampa Simpson tells a story about life before television. However, his story incorporates a bunch of television shows such as: Beverly Hills 90210, The Waltons, The Brady Bunch, The Partridge Family and Leave it to Beaver.

A visit to the Simpson house results in a painful, yet hilarious, injury to Krusty, so he becomes a houseguest. This leaves the Simpsons to fend off a flock of lawyers by broadcasting the show from their own home.
Lisa and Martin have a poetry battle.
The Presidential candidates come to Springfield.
Ned takes Marge ballroom dancing.
After a disaster at the nuclear power plant, Mr. Burns must house the whole town at Burns Manor because it is the only place above the poisonous mushroom cloud.
Ned Flanders goes bad.
After Mr. Burns wastes millions on an unsuccessful advertising campaign to make him more popular, he creates a reality TV show where the winner will take over Mr. Burns' job for a day.
Lisa joins Otto's band, Otto and the Screaming Whiners.
When Bart turns tattletale on Dolph, Jimbo, Kearney, and Nelson on national TV, he becomes the target of death threats.
Mr. Burns tests his Rejuvenator Ray on Homer Simpson, resulting in Homer growing to colossal proportions.
Mr. Burns takes Homer and the kids on his annual treasure hunt.
